registry.description: Anger is one of the most structurally rich inner states in Scripture. The most common Hebrew root literally means nose and face — the flared nostril, the reddened face — before it means anger, embedding the emotion bodily from the start. Heat is the dominant image: burning, kindling, being inflamed. God's anger is extensively described alongside human anger using the same vocabulary. Anger can be provoked — kindled in another — and sits at the intersection of justice, honour, and relational rupture.
